h1: Serving beer at a house party so the last glass tastes fresh
title: Serving beer at a house party | Craft Beer School
desc: Keep beer cold and fresh at a house party until the last glass: buy fresh, chill in ice water, open on demand and look after guests who do not drink.
teaser: The first beer at a party is always cold. Here is how to make sure the one poured at midnight tastes just as good.
standfirst: Beer at a party has a hard life. It sits in the heat, gets opened too early and is poured into whatever cup is closest. A little planning keeps the last glass as fresh as the first.
sections:
The last glass can only be as good as the beer you bought. In Indian heat, beer that sat in a warm shop for weeks has already lost some of its freshness before it reaches your door. Buy from a shop that keeps beer chilled and turns it over quickly. Check the packaging date where there is one. Hoppy beers are best within a few months of packing. Lagers hold a little longer.

Bring it home in a cool bag rather than a hot car boot. A car parked in the sun can easily reach 50 °C inside. An afternoon at that temperature ages beer noticeably.

Get the beer cold before guests arrive, ideally in the fridge overnight. On the day, a cooler box or a large bucket of ice and water keeps it there. Ice and water chill far better than ice alone, because water surrounds every can. A handful of salt makes it colder still for a quick chill, but take beer out once it is cold so it does not start to freeze.

Aim for about 4 °C for lagers. Pale ales and wheat beers can sit slightly warmer. Our guide on chilling beer fast has the details if you are short of time.
Keep the cooler working all night

• Put the cooler in shade, away from the stove, the barbecue and the afternoon sun.
  • Keep the lid closed. Every opening lets warm air in.
  • Do not fill it with all the beer at once. Keep a back-up stock in the fridge and refill the cooler with cold cans as it empties.
  • Drain some meltwater and add fresh ice every couple of hours. Ice is cheap compared with warm beer.

That simple rotation is the main trick. A cooler crammed with warm cans at 7 pm will struggle all evening. A cooler topped up with already cold cans stays cold.

Never pour a row of glasses in advance. Beer starts losing carbonation and freshness from the moment it is opened. In a warm room, a pre-poured glass is flat and warm within half an hour. Open each can or bottle when someone asks for it.

Choose 330 ml cans over 650 ml bottles where you can. Smaller containers get finished while still cold and fresh. Fewer half empty bottles end up abandoned on tables. If you serve from a growler or a party keg, drink it the same evening. Once opened, it stays at its best for only a day or so.

Proper glasses, beer clean and rinsed with cold water just before pouring, make any beer taste better. Smaller glasses of 250 to 330 ml also help, since a small pour is finished before it warms. If you must use disposable cups for a big crowd, choose sturdy ones and pour gently down the side. Our guide to why beer tastes flat from a plastic cup explains what thin cups do.

Skip frozen glasses and ice in the beer. Both water it down and kill the head.

A good party is one where everyone has something good to drink. Put out plenty of cold water, soft drinks, fresh lime soda or non-alcoholic beer in a separate cooler, so guests who do not drink are not fishing among the beer cans. Serve food from the start, not only late in the evening.

Plan how people get home before the party, not after. Nobody should drive after drinking. Have cab numbers ready or arrange lifts with someone who is staying sober. Keep an eye on anyone who seems to be drinking too fast and quietly offer them water or food.

A simple way to plan ice: fill the cooler about one third with ice, add the cans, then top with water until they are nearly covered. For a day-long gathering in summer, plan to replace much of that ice at least once. It is a rough rule, but it is better than running out at 9 pm. Running a party well is like running a small bar: cold, fresh and clean beats a long beer list every time.

Before your next gathering, pick two or three beers instead of six, buy them fresh, chill them overnight and set up one cooler for beer and one for everything else. Keep a back-up stock in the fridge and refill the cooler as you go. The last glass will thank you.
faqs: How do you keep beer cold at a party?
Chill it in the fridge beforehand, then keep it in a shaded cooler of ice and water. Refill the cooler with cold cans from the fridge as it empties.
Should I pour beer into glasses before guests arrive?
No. Open and pour beer as people ask for it. Pre-poured beer goes flat and warm quickly.
Cans or bottles for a party?
Smaller cans are usually better. They chill fast, get finished while still cold and are safer than glass outdoors.
What should I offer guests who do not drink?
Cold water, soft drinks, fresh lime soda or non-alcoholic beer in a separate cooler, plus food from the start.
